 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 06, 2026, 08:31:43 IST SUMMARY Gold Rate Today On Dhanteras 2026 Live Updates: Gold and silver prices are closely tracked by buyers on Dhanteras every year since the day is considered to be auspicious for buying the precious metals. Gold and silver prices have corrected from the lifetime highs seen in January this year, but are still higher than last year’s Diwali and festive season. 
 Jewellers are anticipating a 20-30% increase in the value of gold and silver sales on Dhanteras this Friday, even though prices have retreated sharply from the peaks recorded in January. 
 Dhanteras is regarded as one of the most auspicious occasions in the Hindu calendar for purchasing precious metals. 
 Which way are gold and silver prices headed on Dhanteras 2026? Track TOI’s live blog for latest coverage: Live Events 
 LIVE RATES · INDIA ⟳ 8:56:21 am Gold Rate 22K gold/gm ₹ 13,401 Silver Rate price/10gm ₹ 2,101 Platinum Rate price/10gm ₹ 42,390 08:27 (IST) Nov 06 Gold Rate Today: Recent gold correction to help sales Sachin Jain, Regional CEO (India) at the World Gold Council, said the recent price correction has encouraged consumers to buy jewellery.
 Families planning weddings over the next three to six months could bring forward their purchases to take advantage of current prices, he said. Jain expects demand to remain strong across product categories, ranging from premium jewellery to gold coins and bars.
 07:53 (IST) Nov 06 Gold Rate Today: Jewellery demand Jewellery retailers are also introducing promotional offers and schemes to encourage consumers to make purchases during the festive period.
 Senco Gold Managing Director and CEO Suvankar Sen said the company is aiming to achieve growth of more than 20% during the festive season. 
 According to him, consumers are increasingly willing to experiment with different designs and gold caratages, while continuing to focus on quality, value and versatility. Demand for diamond jewellery is growing by 25-30%, he added.
 07:52 (IST) Nov 06 Gold Rate Today: Demand for gold GJC Vice Chairman Avinash Gupta said gold and silver purchases are being driven by both wedding requirements and investment considerations. Families are choosing gold for the main wedding ceremony, while silver jewellery and other articles are being bought for additional rituals.
 For gold, Gupta expects sales value to increase by 15-20%, with volumes remaining at the previous year's level.
 "The market had witnessed a slowdown over the past six months amid rising gold and silver prices, coupled with the Prime Minister's appeal to citizens to refrain from purchasing gold," he said.
 He added that lightweight jewellery is becoming increasingly popular. Even wedding purchases are shifting towards 18-karat gold jewellery.
 07:51 (IST) Nov 06 Silver Rate Today: Silver in focus Silver continues to find favour with younger consumers because it is relatively affordable and available in a wider variety of designs. Jewellers expect sales volumes to remain unchanged from last year, while sales value could rise by around 30%.
 GJC Vice Chairman Avinash Gupta offered a more upbeat assessment of silver demand. He said the industry is anticipating a 10% year-on-year increase in volumes following a price correction of nearly 50%.
 07:50 (IST) Nov 06 Gold Price Today: Sentiment dampeners With Dhanteras falling early in the month, on November 6, consumers are likely to have received their salaries by the time they make purchases. However, inflationary pressures arising from geopolitical tensions, along with drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, could dampen consumer sentiment.
 "In value terms, sales are likely to grow by 20-30 per cent," All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) Chairman Rajesh Rokde told PTI. "We are expecting flat growth in terms of volume compared to last year."
 07:50 (IST) Nov 06 Gold Rate Today: Tepid buying? India is the world's second-largest consumer of gold and ranks among the biggest gold-importing countries globally, behind China.
 But this festive season, gold purchases are expected to remain unchanged from a year earlier as buyers opt for lighter jewellery and products that require smaller investments.

This compares with the record high of Rs 1,83,000 recorded on January 29, 2026. Despite the correction, gold remains significantly more expensive than it was during Dhanteras last year, when the price stood at Rs 1,32,400 on October 18.
Silver has seen a steeper decline from its January peak. Prices have dropped 52% from Rs 4,04,500 per kg on January 29 to Rs 1,94,500 per kg. However, the metal continues to trade above its Dhanteras 2025 price of Rs 1,70,000 per kg.
